items.why: A record 10 tankers were struck in the Strait of Hormuz between Sep 28 and Oct 4, choking traffic, and Hurricane Isais forced Gulf Coast producers to curtail output. Reports of possible resumed US operations against Iran added to supply fear.
Volatility rose as stocks slipped for a second day after record highs, with oil and yields spiking.

Record Q3 deliveries beat forecasts, but investors worried the rush was pulled forward by the federal EV tax credit expiring at the end of September. A delayed EU vote on Full Self-Driving approval also weighed.
AI chip stocks fell as rising oil and a 10-year yield near 5.30% pulled investors from growth names. Even strong TSMC revenue results were ignored amid bond-yield and crude concerns.

market_note: WTI surging on Strait of Hormuz tanker attacks and a Gulf hurricane; 10Y yield near 5.30%.
summary: Stocks slipped Thursday as oil jumped more than 4% to above $92, reviving inflation fears and pushing the 10-year yield toward a 24-year high. AI-linked chip stocks led the decline.
